title: Jeff Porcaro - Wikipedia
notes: Jeffrey Thomas Porcaro, born 1 April 1954, Hartford, Connecticut; died 5 August 1992, Los Angeles, aged 38. Son of the session percussionist Joe Porcaro, from whom he took lessons from seven; brothers Mike (bass) and Steve (keyboards), both in Toto. At seventeen his first professional job, Sonny & Cher's touring band. Named Jim Keltner and Jim Gordon as his idols. Steely Dan's Katy Lied (1975) and others (Pretzel Logic's Parker's Band beside Gordon; Gaucho). Co-founded Toto with Steve Porcaro, Steve Lukather and David Paich: Toto (1978) to Kingdom of Desire (1992, posthumous). Sessions: Boz Scaggs' Silk Degrees (1976), four tracks of Michael Jackson's Thriller, Dire Straits' On Every Street (1991), Bruce Springsteen's Human Touch (1992), many others. The Rosanna groove: Purdie's half-time shuffle blended with Bonham's Fool in the Rain, 'while keeping a Bo Diddley beat on the bass drum'; described on a Star Licks instructional video. Gear: Gretsch early, then Yamaha, later Pearl; Paiste (endorsed) and Zildjian; Regal Tip signature sticks; Remo heads; DW pedals. Modern Drummer Hall of Fame, 1993. AllMusic: 'arguably the most highly regarded studio drummer in rock from the mid-'70s to the early '90s.' The coroner's ruling on his death is disputed by his family and friends.

title: Jeff Porcaro, instructional video (Star Licks Master Session, 1988), as posted to YouTube
notes: His own words, read from the video's captions (the Rosanna part also posted as bPS9yMYMf8Y). On the hats: eighths with 'an inner lope', an 'inner dynamic up and down'; FM tried in sixteenths, 'too busy', then eighths. Sixteenths single-handed: 'a lot smoother feel' than hand to hand, which on Michael McDonald's I Keep Forgettin' 'sounded just too stiff and staccato'. Matched grip. The bass drum on the toe and the ball of the foot, sliding up into the pedal. Hold the Line: from Sly and the Family Stone's Hot Fun in the Summertime, triplets on the hats, the kick on the downbeat of one and the last triplet of the second beat, snare on two and four, 'like a shuffle Charleston figure', the hat opened on the last triplet of four. The shuffle 'I used on Lido Shuffle and Black Friday': hats on the first and last triplet of each beat, snare on two and four, the kick on the first and last triplets of beats one and three and the last triplets of two and four, 'a ghost note after each backbeat'. Rosanna: 'I stole that beat from listening to two records': Home at Last and Babylon Sisters (Bernard Purdie) and John Bonham on Fool in the Rain; 'I added the Bo Diddley figure. It's a shuffle Bo Diddley figure.' Hats on the first and last note of each triplet, the left hand ghosting the middle one, the backbeat on the third beat, 'the Bo Diddley shuffle bass drum figure'. Shot on a black kit with chrome hardware and a rack, Paiste cymbals; Mike Porcaro and David Garfield in the rhythm section; Joe Porcaro credited.

title: bonedo.de, 'Die besten Drummer der Welt: Jeff Porcaro - The King of Shuffle'
notes: Quotes him: 'I hate Shuffles!'; 'I've never done a solo in my life... I just like playing time'; 'My time sucks!'; studio advice, 'You'd better just play time. Period! Really good time. And make it tasty.' Single-handed sixteenths on the hats. Influences Jim Gordon, Jim Keltner, Harvey Mason, Steve Gadd: 'I copied Gordon and Keltner and all these guys.' Kits: Slingerland, a black Camco, Ludwig; Ludwig live 1977-82, mostly Gretsch in the studio; Pearl from 1982, three rack toms and a 22-inch bass drum, co-developing the DR-1 rack. Paiste 602 and 2002, Signature from 1989; a 14-inch 602 Heavy hi-hat and a 20-inch 602 Medium ride. Satisfied with one session only, Steely Dan's FM.

title: Rosanna (song) - Wikipedia
notes: A half-time shuffle with ghost notes, from the Purdie shuffle, Bonham's Fool in the Rain and the Bo Diddley beat; Porcaro cited Steely Dan's Home at Last. Recorded 1981 at Sunset Sound and Record One; the basic rhythm track in one day. Personnel: Jeff Porcaro drums, Lenny Castro percussion, David Hungate bass.

title: Africa (Toto song) - Wikipedia
notes: Porcaro set up a bass drum, snare and hi-hat, Lenny Castro a conga beside him; no click; they 'played for five minutes on tape' and marked 'the best two bars'. Written by David Paich and Jeff Porcaro. Recorded June 1981, Sunset Sound. Personnel: Jeff Porcaro drums, cowbell, gong, additional percussion; Lenny Castro congas, shakers; Joe Porcaro bass marimba.

title: Toto (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 October 1978, Columbia; recorded October 1977 to June 1978 at Studio 55, Davlen and Sunset Sound; produced by Toto. Hold the Line, Georgy Porgy (Lukather and Cheryl Lynn singing), I'll Supply the Love and Child's Anthem by David Paich. Jeff Porcaro drums; Lenny Castro percussion.

title: Hydra (Toto album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 26 October 1979, Columbia; recorded summer 1979 at Sunset Sound; produced by Toto, Tom Knox and Reggie Fisher. St. George and the Dragon by Bobby Kimball and David Paich. Jeff Porcaro drums, percussion.

title: Toto IV - Wikipedia
notes: Released 29 March 1982, Columbia; recorded June 1981 to January 1982 at Sunset Sound and Record One; produced by Toto. Rosanna by David Paich; Africa by Paich and Jeff Porcaro. Jeff Porcaro drums, percussion; Lenny Castro congas, percussion.

title: The Seventh One - Wikipedia
notes: Released 8 February 1988, Columbia; recorded at The Complex and The Manor; produced by Toto, George Massenburg and Bill Payne. Pamela by David Paich and Joseph Williams. Jeff Porcaro drums, percussion.

title: Silk Degrees - Wikipedia
notes: Boz Scaggs. Released 18 February 1976, Columbia; recorded at Davlen and Hollywood Sound Recorders; produced by Joe Wissert. Lido Shuffle and Lowdown by Scaggs and David Paich. Jeff Porcaro the only drummer credited; David Hungate bass; Joe Porcaro percussion on two tracks.

title: Katy Lied - Wikipedia
notes: Steely Dan. Released 24 March 1975, ABC; recorded November 1974 to January 1975 at ABC Recording Studios, Los Angeles; produced by Gary Katz. Jeff Porcaro drums on every track but Any World (That I'm Welcome To), which is Hal Blaine. Black Friday opens it.

title: Beat It - Wikipedia
notes: Michael Jackson, Thriller (1982); single 21 February 1983. Recorded October 1982 at Westlake and Hayvenhurst; produced by Quincy Jones and Jackson. Jeff Porcaro drums; Jackson a 'drum case beater'. After Eddie Van Halen's solo edits upset the timecode, Porcaro and Steve Lukather re-cut the basic tracks round the vocal and the solo.

title: Hot Fun in the Summertime - Wikipedia
notes: Sly and the Family Stone, released 21 July 1969. Personnel: 'Greg Errico - drums'.
